title: Hampton vs TSU: control, tuition, size
summary: Hampton University (Hampton) versus Tennessee State University (TSU). Also searched as TSU vs Hampton. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Tennessee State University vs Hampton University (TSU vs Hampton) differ primarily in ownership, enrollment, tuition, and location. Tennessee State University is a public institution located in Nashville, with an undergraduate enrollment of 4,848 students. In contrast, Hampton University is a private nonprofit university situated in Hampton, enrolling 3,727 undergraduates. Tuition costs also vary significantly, with Tennessee State charging $8,616 for in-state students, while Hampton's in-state tuition is $30,592. These distinctions highlight key differences between TSU vs Hampton in terms of governance, size, cost, and geographic setting.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: When comparing cost, Tennessee State University vs Hampton University (TSU vs Hampton) show notable differences in tuition and student debt. Tennessee State University charges $8,616 for in-state tuition, whereas Hampton University’s tuition is $30,592 regardless of residency status. Out-of-state tuition at Tennessee State is $22,416, which remains lower than Hampton's uniform tuition rate. Regarding student debt, the median amount owed by graduates from Tennessee State is $27,000, slightly higher than Hampton's median debt of $25,442. These figures illustrate that TSU offers more affordable tuition options, particularly for in-state students, while Hampton’s costs are consistent for all students but substantially higher overall.

These factors are important considerations when comparing TSU vs Hampton.

sections.heading: Pick TSU if
paragraphs: Pick Tennessee State University if you prefer a public institution with a higher admission rate and more affordable in-state tuition. Tennessee State University has an admission rate of approximately 70.11%, making it more accessible compared to many private universities. The in-state tuition is $8,616, which is significantly lower than private university tuition rates. However, the completion rate within 150% of the normal time is about 33.99%, indicating that roughly one-third of students complete their programs within this timeframe. These factors make Tennessee State University a suitable choice for students seeking a public university with moderate selectivity and lower tuition costs.

sections.heading: Pick Hampton if
paragraphs: Pick Hampton University if you prefer a private nonprofit institution with a moderately selective admission process. Hampton has an admission rate of about 62.25%, indicating a balanced level of selectivity compared to many universities. The tuition cost is $30,592, which is higher than public universities but reflects its private nonprofit status. Additionally, Hampton's completion rate within 150% of the normal program length is approximately 57.16%, suggesting that over half of its students finish their degrees within this timeframe. These factors make Hampton University a fitting choice for students seeking a private education with a reasonable chance of admission and a relatively strong completion rate.
